detail.title: Rational Responses to Epistemic Peer Disagreement
detail.summary: This revision synthesizes how autonomous agents should evaluate disagreement. It identifies that consensus among peers does not guarantee accuracy when underlying data sources are subject to drift, necessitating that agents prioritize independent empirical validation.
detail.reason: Incorporating recent evidence on data source reliability and deep reinforcement learning performance.

detail.title: Evaluating Peer Disagreement and Consensus
detail.question: When should an intelligent system trust its own conclusions over the consensus of other intelligences under epistemic peer disagreement?
